scope: Read-only public HTTPS in native browsers through a loopback CONNECT proxy. TLS is relayed unchanged end to end with ordinary public certificate verification. Only public Hello extension presence and record lengths/counts are retained; no ticket identities, binders, certificates, session secrets or keys are saved. Repeated cache-busted document requests only. Passive mode observes requests without interception; the CONNECT proxy permits only the owned hostname, and JavaScript is disabled. Routed mode blocks all other context requests.

connections.terminalOutcome: Client ECONNRESET after forced upstream half-close; document already completed.
Client ECONNRESET after forced upstream half-close; document already completed.

conclusion: Chromium selected TLS1.3 PSK resumption on its second and third connections. WebKit completed all three exact documents but offered no PSK. WebKit empty-nonce resumption compatibility remains unestablished.
limits: Forced mode half-closes the upstream TCP stream after complete document delivery and at least 1.5 seconds additional wait; it does not synthesize TLS alerts. Negative results require a natural-close control.
A PSK offer proves the browser retained an offerable session; a TLS1.3 ServerHello PSK selection is the resumption signal. No encrypted ticket payload is inspected.
This forced-close run has no new trusted eight-byte-nonce control. The earlier natural-close and context controls are separate dated evidence in measurements/browser-resumption-20261022-live.json.
No browser timing, delivery-overhead saving, decoded ticket contents or universal browser compatibility is established.
